hints: Look at the functional group at the end of each molecule. Which ones have a carboxyl (-COOH) group and which one has only alcohol (-OH) groups?
Remember a carboxyl group is -C(=O)-OH, so it always contains a C=O double bond, while glycerol is a triol with three C-OH single bonds only.
walkthrough:
**Recall what C=O means**

Think carbonyl. A C=O double bond is found in carboxylic acids as part of -COOH, and in other carbonyl groups. It is not found in simple alcohol C-OH groups.

**Check each molecule**

1. Amino acids have an amine group plus a carboxyl group (-COOH), so yes to C=O.

2. Fatty acids have a long hydrocarbon chain plus a carboxyl group (-COOH), so yes to C=O.

3. Glycerol is propane-1,2,3-triol with three -OH groups and no C=O, so no.

**Pick the combination**

Only 1 and 2 contain C=O. That matches option B, 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because glycerol (3) has only C-O and C-OH single bonds, with no C=O, so 1, 2 and 3 cannot all be correct.
options.B: Correct because both amino acids and fatty acids contain a carboxyl -COOH group which includes a C=O bond, while glycerol does not.
options.C: Incorrect because although amino acids (1) are correct, glycerol (3) has no C=O and fatty acids (2) are wrongly left out.
options.D: Incorrect because although fatty acids (2) are correct, glycerol (3) has no C=O and amino acids (1) are wrongly left out.
